text: Groundhog Day: if the groundhog sees its shadow, six more weeks of winter
Mackerel sky and mares' tails make tall ships carry low sails
Rain before seven, fine by eleven
Red sky at night, shepherd's delight
Ring around the moon, rain soon
St Swithin's Day, if thou dost rain, for forty days it will remain

name: Red-sky point 150 km west of London

coordinateSource.title: Wikipedia coordinates API
coordinateSource.note: Derived: same latitude as location-london, longitude -0.13 - 150 / (111.32 * cos(51.51 deg)) = -2.2948, rounded to 2 dp

title: Groundhog Day: if the groundhog sees its shadow, six more weeks of winter
statement: In Punxsutawney, Punxsutawney Phil's published call (shadow = six more weeks of winter) matches whether 3 February to 16 March is colder than its 1991-2020 normal more often than chance.

title: Mackerel sky and mares' tails make tall ships carry low sails
statement: In Plymouth, mornings with abundant high cloud and little low cloud at 09:00 are more often followed within 24 hours by rain or a strong gust than mornings in general.

title: Rain before seven, fine by eleven
statement: In London, days with rain between 05:00 and 07:00 local time are more often dry from 11:00 to 12:00 than days in general.

title: Red sky at night, shepherd's delight
statement: In London, evenings with a clear western horizon and mid or high cloud overhead at sunset are more often followed by a dry next day than evenings in general.

title: Red sky at night, shepherd's delight
statement: In London, evenings with a clear western horizon and mid or high cloud overhead at sunset are more often followed by a dry next day than evenings in general.

title: Ring around the moon, rain soon
statement: In London, nights with thin high cloud, little low cloud and a bright moon above the horizon are more often followed by rain 24 to 48 hours later than nights in general.

title: St Swithin's Day, if thou dost rain, for forty days it will remain
statement: In London, years with rain on 15 July have more rainy days from 16 July to 24 August than years with a dry 15 July.

reason: Found while writing the fetcher, which refuses to fetch any point whose coordinates are not inside a verified lock. consequence: v1 is superseded and will never be tested. v2 takes v1's slot in the six-member Holm family; the other five locks still list the v1 id, and this deviation is the mapping. Filed before any weather data was fetched.

why: suncalc 2.1.0, the version the lock names, reports getMoonPosition().altitude in degrees (its index.d.ts: 'All angles are in degrees').
effect: None. The threshold is 0 and the comparator is '>', so the predicate is identical in either unit. The runner asserts the locked threshold is exactly 0.
whyNotADeviation: A deviation records a change that could alter a result (deviation 001: unhashed coordinates). This label cannot change any count, p-value or verdict. Filing a deviation for it would dilute what a deviation means, so it is disclosed as an erratum and the locked hash is unchanged.
